entries.reason: Framework-agnostic assertion-site probe for test-quality scoring; a framework's assert call has no AST node type this indexer exposes and includes() cannot express the optional `.word(` form.
Detects expect( sites across Jest/Vitest/Mocha/Chai; statement-level source evidence, no AST equivalence exists.
Chai should-style assertions are property accesses (should.equal) that only a pattern can recognise generically.
Matcher methods (toBe/toThrow/rejects...) appear after an arbitrary receiver expression, so the matcher method call itself is the only stable anchor.
Promise settlement evidence in assertions; two words with word boundaries, matched across any framework.
Error-path evidence: `try {` requires the brace as the next non-space token, which a plain includes('try') cannot enforce without false positives.
toThrow/throws are matcher/property names whose position cannot be found by string operations without reimplementing word boundaries.
Error-path evidence: `catch (` requires the call parenthesis, which includes('catch') cannot distinguish from the keyword followed by an identifier.
Data-driven test detection spans it.each/test.each/describe template literals/%s/$var; five alternative shapes with no common prefix.
Counts comment lines, which requires an alternation for line start, blank-prefix and three comment styles; character scanning would reimplement the same state machine.
Descriptive test names: a minimum name length inside quoted/backticked first argument, which needs the quote alternation and repetition counts.
Mock evidence: jest/sinon/vi fn/spyOn/mock plus mockImplementation and nock( across four frameworks; the alternatives share no prefix.
